root_cause.text: A race in the i915 GT heartbeat code used non-atomic read-and-clear operations on `engine->heartbeat.systole`, allowing the heartbeat worker and `intel_engine_park_heartbeat()` to both observe the same request pointer and call `i915_request_put()` twice on it.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit explicitly states the worker "reads `engine->heartbeat.systole` and calls `i915_request_put()` on it when the request is complete, but clears the pointer in a separate, non-atomic step," and the patch replaces these paths with `xchg(&engine->heartbeat.systole, NULL)` in both `heartbeat()` and `intel_engine_park_heartbeat()` so only one caller can obtain the non-NULL pointer.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The CVE/commit explicitly states the worker "reads `engine->heartbeat.systole` and calls `i915_request_put()` on it when the request is complete, but clears the pointer in a separate, non-atomic step," and the patch replaces these paths with `xchg(&engine->heartbeat.systole, NULL)` in both `heartbeat()` and `intel_engine_park_heartbeat()` so only one caller can obtain the non-NULL pointer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Atomically clear and recheck `heartbeat.systole` so completed requests are released safely without dropping unfinished ones due to races.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a direct read of `engine->heartbeat.systole` followed by conditional clearing with an atomic `xchg(&engine->heartbeat.systole, NULL)`. It also changes the logic so that if a request was retrieved, completed requests are released with `i915_request_put(rq)`, while incomplete requests are written back to `engine->heartbeat.systole` instead of leaving the field cleared.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this atomically detaches the `systole` request pointer before inspecting it, preventing races with concurrent accesses to that field. It also avoids losing an in-flight request by restoring it when it has not yet completed, while still cleaning up completed requests properly.

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard heartbeat systole cleanup by atomically clearing the pointer and only dropping the request reference when one exists.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a single call to i915_request_put(fetch_and_zero(&engine->heartbeat.systole)) with a braced block that first assigns rq = xchg(&engine->heartbeat.systole, NULL) and then conditionally calls i915_request_put(rq) only if rq is non-NULL.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the heartbeat systole pointer is still atomically cleared, but the request reference is now released only when a valid request was actually present, avoiding an unconditional put on a possibly NULL result and making the cleanup path explicitly safe.

intent_record.intent_summary: Guard heartbeat parking against a NULL systole request by explicitly clearing the pointer and only releasing it when present.
intent_record.what: The function intel_engine_park_heartbeat() was changed so that, when cancel_delayed_work(&engine->heartbeat.work) succeeds, it now enters a block that declares a local struct i915_request *rq, assigns it using xchg(&engine->heartbeat.systole, NULL), and conditionally calls i915_request_put(rq) only if rq is non-NULL, replacing the previous single call to i915_request_put(fetch_and_zero(&engine->heartbeat.systole)).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this preserves the behavior of cancelling pending heartbeat work and clearing the systole request pointer, but makes the pointer exchange explicit and avoids calling i915_request_put() with a NULL value. This prevents a potential invalid put on a NULL request while still safely dropping the reference when a request was present.

vuln_statements.explanation: This non-atomic read of engine->heartbeat.systole is the core of the race: the heartbeat worker can load the request pointer while a concurrent path such as intel_engine_park_heartbeat() also observes the same pointer, leading both sides to operate on the same request reference.

This separate non-atomic clear is decoupled from the earlier read, so the read-and-clear is not atomic. A concurrent thread can race between these operations, observe the same request pointer, and later trigger a duplicate release.

This reference drop becomes unsafe because it is performed on a request obtained through the racy non-atomic read of heartbeat.systole; if another racing path also observed the same pointer, both paths can call i915_request_put() on it.
